report.board_note: The board is fragmented, not unified, this morning. The international reference legs behind bullion and copper fell sharply overnight — silver down 5.38%, copper down 4.95%, gold down 1.17% — while the energy references rose, crude up 6.69% and natural gas up 0.43%. The four LME-priced base metals (zinc, aluminium, lead, nickel) carry no implied open at all: that is a refusal by design, since LME publishes before MCX closes, and it covers four of the board's nine names. Where an implied open does exist, none of it is actually overnight — every Tier A implied-open span reads 'over 2 calendar days — NOT overnight', because the rupee leg last moved from 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-10, two calendar days apart, even though each reference leg itself is a genuine one-session overnight move. The rupee's own move over that span, +0.79% (INR weaker against the dollar), is real but it is smaller than most of the reference moves it compounds with — for gold, silver, copper and crude the reference leg ran 1.17% to 6.69%, dwarfing the rupee — with one exception: natural gas's own reference move was just 0.43%, smaller than the rupee leg, so there the rupee is the larger of the two legs. On balance the rupee is a contributing factor today, not the story; the international leg is doing the driving in four of five Tier A names. On the bullion side, the Indian import premium shows a small, ordinary gold discount (1.25 percentage points below parity, a z of -0.13 over 198 sessions) against a firmer, richer silver premium (3.03 percentage points above parity, a z of 0.29 over 218 sessions) — the contrast between an unremarkable gold read and a comparatively rich silver read is itself the finding, not either number alone.

report.board_note: The board for this run ships no news or article data at all — there is no news array anywhere in scan.json, so this is a positioning-only morning for all nine instruments, not a choice made after reading the wires. That silence is most interesting against CRUDEOIL, SILVER and COPPER, which are showing the three largest overnight moves on the board (an implied open of +7.5% on CRUDEOIL, -4.6% on SILVER, -4.2% on COPPER, each built from a genuinely overnight international leg per intl_span_label) with nothing stored to explain any of them: positioning-led, no catalyst, and the size of the move makes the absence worth flagging rather than assuming. GOLD and NATURALGAS show smaller implied opens (-0.39% and +1.21%) and are equally uncovered. The four Tier B metals — ZINC, ALUMINIUM, LEAD, NICKEL — have no implied open on the board at all (Tier B carries no international reference leg) and, consistent with the standing expectation for base metals, no coverage either. DXY does not appear anywhere in this scan.json, so no dollar read is possible this morning; EIA prints for CRUDEOIL and NATURALGAS are on the board but both are dated 2026-09-04, a week old against an 2026-09-11 board date, and consensus is not available regardless.

report.board_note: The board leans toward unwinding, not building: six of the nine instruments carry an open-interest state that reads as an exit rather than an entry — long liquidation in gold, copper, zinc, aluminium and lead, and short covering in nickel — while only three show fresh money actually arriving: crude oil with new longs, and silver and natural gas both with new shorts. That lean is not uniform in direction, though — it is an unwind across bullion and base metals sitting alongside fresh conviction in energy and silver, which is a fragmented morning, not a single-direction one. The clearest outlier is crude oil: it is the only instrument on the board where open interest built on a rally, the one unambiguous case of fresh buying rather than an exit, and it carries the single largest open-interest addition on the board in contract terms. Natural gas is the other instrument to flag on its own terms: its open-interest state reads as fresh shorts (price down, open interest up), yet its own overnight and international reference moves are both positive, an internal disagreement the board does not resolve and this report will not either.

report.board_note: Six of the nine instruments sit under one ATR from their nearest level this morning — gold 0.93 ATR from support at 149,665, silver 0.42 ATR from support at 231,811, copper 0.66 ATR from support at 1,361.1, zinc 0.89 ATR from resistance at 424.15, lead 0.62 ATR from support at 195.5, and nickel 0.45 ATR from support at 1,596.0 — so the board reads coiled rather than extended; the three that sit further out are crude oil (2.52 ATR to its only stated support, with no resistance level on the board at all), natural gas (1.27 ATR to support, 1.78 to resistance) and aluminium (1.53 ATR to support, 1.95 to resistance). Volatility does not split cleanly by data tier: today's range is expanding relative to its recent average for gold (2,880.86 vs 2,708.68), copper (17.53 vs 16.65) and zinc (10.06 vs 7.43), compressed for silver (5,390.71 vs 5,871.88), crude oil (305.36 vs 356.80), aluminium (4.44 vs 5.16) and lead (1.60 vs 2.51), and roughly unremarkable for natural gas (8.73 vs 8.78) and nickel (20.29 vs 20.84). The exception is zinc, which combines the widest volatility expansion on the board (today's range roughly 35% above its recent average) with a resistance level under one ATR away, making it the one instrument where a near level and an expanding day line up; crude oil is a second, smaller exception in that the board carries no resistance level for it at all, leaving only a support read. On the cross-instrument ratios: gold sits at 65.08 rupees-per-gram against silver, normalised to rupees per gram from the 10-gram and kilogram quotes, a percentile of 0.5286 over a 250-session back-adjusted continuous window — roughly the middle of its recent range. Crude oil sits at 35.94 as quoted (rupees per barrel over rupees per mmBtu, a genuinely cross-unit reading), a percentile of 0.862 over the same 250-session window — high in its recent range.
